Technically they call it an "Altruistic donor" but I feel like that sounds all haughtly and annoying. The gist of it is that I got a kidney taken out to be put into a random person on the donor list. (well not random, but you know).

So do ask me anything. I'd type more here but I feel like that kind of defeats the purpose! And forgive me if I'm a little slow to reply (Have class soon), I'll get to everyone eventually!

For pain wise, not bad. I think surgeries always have their pain hyped up as a precaution or something. They always used "It may be surprisingly painful". The word "Surprisingly" always. It stuck out to me, it was so vague but also worrying lol. But basically I was up an able to walk around about a day-or-so after. Didn't have too much recovery pain but it did hurt to get up or learn and all for a bit (They make the incisions through your front now actually!). So all in all its not too bad. I think taking the catheter out was the most stressful. I had done it before, not an experience I was looking forward to again.

Other people have a little worse recovery. A big one I'd read about online is that one in a couple hundred guys will get these really swollen like, orange sized testicles that hurt like hell and are obviously not fun to have, but I didn't have to deal with that thankfully! (Its caused I believe by the nicking some nerve near the kidneys I believe?)

Definitely something I'd do again. ...well not now, I only have one kidney. But it was a worthwhile experience!
Are there really any major side effect.from only having one kidney.

Actually no, not really. A lot of people assume I can't drink or similar. But the one kidney compensates for the lost one, and you really don't need the power of two for the most part anyway.

I do cut down on sodium a bit which they recommended. Mostly just wanting to avoid kidney stones among other things. But I suppose thats a good thing to do anyway!
